t: There's no house to see here now. Tavistock House, long demolished, was the London home of Charles Dickens and his family from 1851 to 1860. In those years he wrote Bleak House, Hard Times, Little Dorrit and A Tale of Two Cities, and staged amateur theatricals at the house. His wife Catherine kept a large household and raised ten children; the two separated in 1858. The Regency developer James Burton is named as its designer. Later it belonged to William and Georgina Weldon, whose lodger, the composer Charles Gounod, wrote part of his opera Polyeucte here.
